To a child of Castrum Kremnos, the battlefield is where one comes alive. The wanton destruction is sweeter than ambrosia; the bloodied corpses are an encouragement to fight without faltering, for a chance to defy death itself; the screams and cries of the damned and dying are an accompanying melody; and the fear of death warps into a cruel excitement that fuels each strike.

Mydeimos, of course, is no different. From the moment he was old enough to curl his fingers into fists, he has yearned for it. Nine years in the Sea of Souls steeled his desire into something unbreakable to match his undying flesh. Only when fear and pain ceased to have any meaning to him could he prepare himself to walk the path of prophecy.

As he charges back in to strike Nikador's heart once more, he reminds himself of his many trials. Fighting against this shameful creature is not as difficult as anything else he has endured, or so he tells himself. He has long since dissociated himself from reality--if he took a moment to consider his exhaustion, he would immediately collapse.

His body may be undying, but he is not immortal. He needs food, water, and rest. The more desperate for reprieve he becomes, the worse he fares. He has erred many times over the course of this fight, and the weight of his mistakes is not a burden he can shoulder for much longer.

In the Evernight, it is impossible to determine how long this has lasted. Days must've passed, perhaps even weeks. Time has lost all meaning. The world around him is nonsensical--all that matters is his target.

Phainon and the outlander Dan Heng joined him a while ago, but Mydei is not in the state of mind to acknowledge either of them. They exist as blurs in his periphery, easily ignored in favor of his target.

He and Phainon have fought together many times, and such excursions are often enjoyable, as they trade quips and compete to see who can vanquish the most foes. They may even trade blows with each other, just to test each others' steel. This, however, is not such a lighthearted affair. Even if he had the strength to speak, he would not. The slaying of a titan is always a solemn dance, and Nikador is the beating heart of his homeland. Their end means the end of Castrum Kremnos.

But of course, he left this place long ago. He has no need for tears. When the fabric of reality warps around him, and the Trailblazer returns to the battle, he feels only relief, not sadness. When Nikador's perverse form finally turns to ash, he smiles, for he is finally free.

"Easy now, don't move!" Hyacine warns, holding her arm out to stop Mydei from sitting up, which is his immediate reflex upon waking up in an unfamiliar location. Then, his mind catches up to his body, and he realizes that he's at the infirmary.

He has been here many times, but has never found himself laid upon one of the cots. He didn't know he could be injured enough to warrant such treatment, though in this particular instance, it seems plausible.

Has he been here for long? The notion is disquieting, and he hopes he hasn't. He tries to ask, but his throat is so dry that only a pathetic wheeze comes out. Hyacine notices his plight, and props him up enough to allow him to sip some water.

"Was I out for long?" he finally manages to say, though his voice is still gravelly.

"Oh, just around six hours. I expected you to be asleep for at least a few days, but your constitution always surpasses such expectations. Fantastic as always, my friend!"

A pleasing answer. With one concern settled, he has only one other. "And where is Phainon?"

"He left a while ago. He's been by your bedside since he brought you here, but I sent him home, since he hadn't eaten or slept. He wasn't my patient, yet I still feel some responsibility to look out for his well-being."

Mydei scoffs. "Of course. He worries too much."

It's always like this. Whenever he suffers an injury, Phainon insists that he comes here, even though it is entirely unnecessary, and then accompanies him while he is treated, as if there's something to fear. Ridiculous, truly.

She waves her hand dismissively. "Never mind my choice of words. I think you're close enough for him to worry, no matter the circumstances. It doesn't matter. I've got other patients to tend to, I've already spoken to you for long enough--you need to rest!"

An annoyance, but he can, indeed, wait. And as he expected, the infirmary door swings open with a gentle chime to herald Phainon's return only a few minutes later.

He appears rather unkempt, with pieces of his armor askew and bags under his eyes. As he makes his way over to the cot, his pauldron slips down his shoulder, and he doesn't bother to fix it.

Chapter Notes

Perhaps it is childish of him, but Mydei resolves that he will not go to the Vortex of Genesis to see Phainon off. He doesn't believe his presence will be welcome, not right after they've fought. The tension between them will certainly be noted by Aglaea, and he'd rather not explain to her the entire timeline of events since they returned from Castrum Kremnos. Some matters are private.

He busies himself at the training ground; it isn't as entertaining as going to the Evernight, but it should satisfy him. He eviscerates a squadron of training dummies with a variety of weapons, from spears to short swords to javelins--he even uses a longbow, in hopes that the struggle with its unfamiliarity will distract him.

Then, once the corpses of straw and fabric litter the sand, he goes to the Vortex of Genesis. The uncertainty of Phainon's fate is simply too much for him to bear. The thought of wasting any more time is more unpleasant than whatever he'll face there.

He is not the sort of person to hope for anything. It is an inescapable emotion, but he finds it more troublesome than helpful, so he's always quick to dismiss it. Still, a part of him hopes, with surprising fervor, that he'll find Phainon triumphant. Mydei will waltz in to find all his worries dispelled, as Phainon stands before him a newly-made demigod, proud bearer of Nikador's Coreflame.

Of course, that is not what he's met with. Instead he finds his allies crowded around the basin, with only Phainon absent. For a moment, that hopeful part of him wonders if the ceremony has not yet begun, and Phainon is just behind schedule.

But the Lance of Fury's constellation is illuminated, indicating only one outcome.

"Still too late, huh..." he sighs, unable to mask the dejection in his tone. This is why he dislikes hope; when it is dashed, it makes failure more difficult to swallow.

"Phainon said you weren't coming," Stelle comments, "I thought it was because you were still recovering... I guess you're better now, huh."

"Of course I've recovered. Did the story of my undying body not sway you? My absence was for another reason, though it seemed increasingly inappropriate. I suppose I should've decided to come earlier, I believe I've missed my chance to bid him good luck."

Castorice nods. "The Coreflame was surrendered, but Lord Phainon's test isn't over yet, unfortunately. The prophecy sent an ambassador. They acknowledged his strength and character, but had doubts concerning the fortitude of his will."

"... I was right to be worried," he mutters, mostly to himself. It is just as he anticipated. If only he could've spoken more eloquently, perhaps he could've avoided this outcome--but there's no point in constructing a perfect fantasy from a past that he cannot change. What's done is done, and now, all they can do is wait.

He considers returning to the training grounds, but since he bothered to come here, he supposes he should try to be personable. He can sulk later. "No matter. I want to formally thank you, outsiders. Were it not for your aid, our campaign against Nikador would have been a hundred times more arduous."

Stelle's eyes widen. "Woah. After all the abuse you hurled my way, I didn't think I'd get a formal thank you! Isn't it nice to be polite?"

Somehow, he finds himself immediately regretting his kindness. "Kremnoans revere strength in battle, but that does not mean we lack all etiquette."

The other outsider, Dan Heng, appears more contemplative. "Mydei, what do you mean when you said you were 'worried'? Did you have reason to anticipate this outcome?"

That question takes him off guard, and he turns to Castorice. "They don't know yet?"

With the camaraderie between the outsiders and Phainon, he expected him to have at least said something about himself, but it appears he wasn't comfortable enough to share, or perhaps he just didn't get the opportunity.

"He's always been tormented by his past. I may not be the right person to tell you about him... We have had our disagreements over it, after all. But if you are to continue fighting with him, I believe it is your right to know."

Perhaps sensing his lingering frustration, Castorice takes over, though she gives him a look that indicates she'll be asking him about it later. He curses himself for not controlling his tone.

The moment the outsiders have left the Vortex, she turns to him. "Did you get into another argument earlier? Phainon seemed unhappy when he came here, and didn't mention why you didn't want to come."

"I would not call it an argument, per se..." He isn't keen to admit that it was, in essence, pillow talk. The other Chrysos Heirs must have an inkling that their relationship goes beyond their partnership in battle, but the longer he can go without explaining it, the better. He doesn't want to invite any extra complications into his life.

"Then what would you call it?"

"... I simply urged him to consider his motives for surrendering the Coreflame, as we all have done."

"Yet you angered him to the extent that he did not want you here for the ceremony."

"I pressed him more intently, as I believed it was pertinent to be aggressive. I didn't anticipate this outcome."

"Were you cruel?"

He doesn't like the way she asks that question. They're teetering on the brink of an argument, and he'd rather not argue with her when Aglaea is standing only a few feet away; she's tending to Trinnon, but she's certainly listening to their conversation. Aglaea aside, he's not exactly in the mood for this.

"I don't..." he pauses to swallow back the hot saliva gathering under his tongue. "I don't know, I wasn't trying to be, but perhaps I was too harsh. I don't think I made things worse."

"You're quite pale, Lord Mydei," Castorice notes , abruptly changing the subject. He would welcome it, but he doesn't want to draw his own attention to his mounting discomfort. Since he arrived here, he's felt an unfamiliar malaise; he thought ignoring it would make it go away--foolish of him, really. It's only gotten worse. What started as a dull cramping in his stomach has progressed to something else that, while entirely foreign to him, is certainly unpleasant.

What might this malaise be? Before he has the chance to mull it over, he's doubled over and vomited on his boots.

So that is what nausea feels like.

"Oh dear," he hears Aglaea say, though he can barely make her words out past the ringing in his ears. Even after his body has ejected most of his stomach contents, he continues to violently retch, bringing up mouthfuls of sour, stinging bile. And then, once there is truly nothing left, he dry heaves.

He isn't sure how long he stands there, hunched over and gripping his abdomen. When he can finally manage to inhale and exhale evenly without gagging, he rights his posture. Of course, Aglaea and Castorice are beside him.

"Do you feel a bit better now?" Aglaea asks, a concerned note in her usually-even tone.

"I believe so... I did not know such a thing could happen to me."

Mydei has vomited before, but only in battle, when an opponent struck him in the right place with enough force. Immortality does not save one from reflexive shock or internal bleeding. Otherwise, his body is incapable of getting sick, so he should have no reason to vomit.

How odd.

"Would you like for me to fetch Hyacine?"

He frowns, debating what response will save him from another visit. "That is unnecessary. I believe my nausea was the result of stress... I've been a bit worried about Phainon, I suppose."

It is as much of an admission as he's willing to make. Thankfully, it appears to be adequate.

"Ah. Well, I suppose there isn't much any of us can do about that but remain steadfast in our faith. If it is of any comfort to you, I am certain he will return, even if his body is unable to accept the Coreflame. The prophecy's ambassador did not seem to be an unreasonable sort."

"I share her sentiment," Castorice adds, "though I believe your affliction may not be... hmm, never mind. I do not think it is my place to say. I believe you should see Hyacine--not urgently, but you should at some point soon."

Her words are so cryptic that he's stuck on how to reply. Even Aglaea seems confused, a rare occurrence.

"I was just seen by her after the battle with Nikador, I believe I'm in top form."

"Then I may be mistaken. Disregard my advice," she says quickly. She doesn't like being put on the spot, and she's clearly uncomfortable. Mydei

doesn't wish to add to her troubles, so he decides not to ask what she meant. If she made a mistake, there is no reason to berate her.

Aglaea hums, a contemplative hand under her chin. "In that case, I suppose I should take Trinnon to get some rest. Mydei, you should rest as well. Excess stress will not better our odds, and it certainly won't hasten Phainon's return."

More rest--the idea isn't thrilling to him, but she's probably right. A quick nap, and perhaps all his problems will be solved.

A quick nap does not solve all his problems, and Castorice's words do not leave his mind.

Over the next few weeks, the feeling of nausea persists, haunting him at nearly every waking hour. He can barely eat--the only foods that don't make him immediately sick are bread and hard tack, and there is no guarantee he won't vomit those up too, so touchy is his stomach.

Certain things are worse. When he attends a victory feast thrown in the outsiders' honor, the wine makes him gag from a single sip, and the mere smell of fish makes him hurry to excuse himself so he can empty his stomach in private.

Is it really stress? He's still worried for Phainon, but at this point, there's no need to get too concerned. Based on what Aglaea said, it seems unlikely that Phainon won't return from his trial. The worst case would be him returning defeated, and Mydei already knows what he must do if that occurs.

He does not wish to take Nikador's Coreflame. It is true that his body is the most willing vessel for it, but it could just as easily destroy him. How easy would it be for him to turn into a worse version of his father, a mad king made unimaginably powerful by the boon of a titan's power. The Kremnoans do not deserve to have their future ripped from them, they should not have to follow their crown prince down that terrible path. For all of them, himself included, there should be something more than strife.

But if Phainon is to fail, then he will sacrifice himself. It is the only other option.

No matter how displeasing that prospect is, he hesitates to blame it for his current ailment. There is more to it than just the nausea, after all. Much more.

The fatigue is the most mortifying. After only a brief training session, he's winded and trembling, barely able to stand upright. Trying to push himself further has, on multiple occasions, caused him to get light headed to the point of collapse.

But the imbalance in his emotions has caused more difficulties. In the course of minutes, his mood may completely change. His temper is more strained than frayed twine. At the last few meetings he's had with the Council, he's gotten into shouting matches. He nearly lost his temper when haggling with the grocer.

Then, there are the stranger occurrences: the irresistible urge to stay in Phainon's house, soaking in his scent; the potent lust which overtakes him at the most inopportune moments, and takes ages to fade, no matter how he tends to himself; the odd cravings he's had for foods he normally detests.

Still, he tries to dismiss it. He cannot get sick, so this affliction isn't real. It must be a product of his mind. Stress is taking its toll on him. Once Phainon returns, he will be as right as rain.

But after three weeks of ignorance, it is finally time to face the music. In the middle of changing, the sight of himself in the mirror, usually so innocuous, makes his blood run cold.

Something is different.

He turns to the side and stares at his figure until he finally comes to terms with it. Undeniably, there is a pronounced roundness to his lower abdomen, and a softening of the muscle there. No matter how he adjusts his pose, or scrubs at his eyes, it remains.

"What the hell," he mutters. He prods at the offending area, finding no give--of course it isn't fat, he's barely been eating as of late, and even his lack of exercise can't bridge the deficit.

How did he not notice this earlier? It didn't come out of nowhere--had he been so intent on denial that he entirely ignored the reality before him? How daft.

I believe you should see Hyacine--not urgently, but you should at some point soon.

Again, those words cross his mind.

Castorice was not mistaken.

Ten minutes later, he steps into Hyacine's infirmary on his own accord. The smell of antiseptic and medicine burns his nose, a hundred times worse than before, and his stomach flips ominously. He grits his teeth. Not now.

"I'll be with you in a moment," Hyacine calls. He sits on one of the tiny waiting room chairs, feeling entirely out of place. When Hyacine comes up to the front, her expression indicates that he looks just as strange as he feels.

"Mydei, my friend, I didn't... ahem, where are my manners... Welcome, come right this way!"

The moment they're in the examination room, she starts pulling the typical supplies out of the cabinet, clearly anticipating another wound to clean and stitch shut. "Without Phainon around, I didn't think you'd be coming here, but--"

"I'm not here for an injury."

Suddenly, he has her full attention. "Oh, I apologize. I wasn't aware that you'd have another reason to see me, but anything can happen, I suppose. Is something the matter?"

"I believe I'm pregnant."

He did not expect to ever utter those words. They feel strange coming from his mouth, like they don't belong to him. Fate's hand has guided him down a violent path, slick with the blood of his family and comrades, and it seems unimaginable that it would grant him something so gentle.

If Hyacine is surprised, she hides it well. Instead, her cheerful, conversational tone is immediately replaced with her professional demeanor. "You'd like for me to run a blood test to confirm? I can certainly do so, but I'd like to hear your symptoms first, just to rule anything else out."

"I cannot get sick, yet I'm constantly fatigued and nauseous. What could cause those symptoms that is not a disease?" He doesn't want to snap at her, but can't bite back his rudeness in time.

"I see. Allow me to draw some blood, then. We'll proceed from there."

It takes twenty minutes for the results, and he is left alone with his thoughts. With no desire to think about anything of consequence, he stares at a painting of the sea that hangs on the wall. He's never liked the ocean, which he supposes makes sense. Not even time has managed to ease the pain of that memory--it is foundational to his being.

But no, he won't let his mind wander, and he forces himself to stare at the painting until his eyes burn from the lack of blinking. Only when Hyacine returns is his concentration broken.

"You're pregnant."

He expects the confirmation to make him feel something. Shouldn't it? Sadness or happiness or dread or anger--something should fill his heart now that the tension is gone.

"I cannot believe I missed this when you were last here! I suppose that's a lesson to me: run blood work as a precaution, even when it seems unnecessary," she continues. Her voice sounds distant, as if she's not standing right in front of him, holding his gaze.

He opens his mouth to respond, but no sound comes out. Another attempt, and he manages a shuddering exhale. He's in shock--why? Kremnoans do not allow their emotions to control them, he's spent his whole life beating that part of him into submission. He shouldn't be frozen by the confirmation of his own suspicions.

Hyacine's demeanor softens, as she must see his turmoil. "If this is unwanted, I will do my best to help you clear the child from your body. To be frank, I'm not sure if it will be possible, not with your constitution, but I have some very potent abortifacients that might work."

All of the battles he's fought since the child's conception--which was certainly during his heat--and all of the injuries he's sustained have insofar not been enough to snuff out its life. He's quite sure that a medication will prove ineffective, even if it comes from a Chrysos Heir.

Regardless, he knows with complete clarity that he doesn't desire that outcome.

He loves Phainon. Gods above, does he love Phainon. He has since the day of their duel, when Mydei tasted defeated for the first time, lying disarmed and prone on the ground, with Phainon's foot planted firmly on his heaving chest. It was as intimate as any proposal. Of course Mydei fell for him. His heart would forever belong to the only man strong enough to take his life.

Perhaps it didn't start then for Phainon, but it did at some point, without a doubt. The lingering touches, the soft looks, the overbearing concern, the years of thoughtful words and abundant care that have added together into a declaration in their own right--that was love, wasn't it?

All this time, they've loved each other, and Mydei only realized it once he couldn't express it anymore. What fools they are, to have loved each other so naturally that it happened without either of them noticing. The most important words remain unsaid.

If only they'd said it sooner, this could all have gone differently. Phainon might be beside him--he'd have demanded Mydei come here ages ago, of course. And he'd be overjoyed, wouldn't he?

At first he'd be scared. The wounds of his past would heighten his fear beyond any normal anxiety. But the idea of a child of his own, a family to live for--his joy would overcome the pain eventually. Even the uncertainty of the future would not make him falter once he found his resolve.

On his own, Mydei doesn't think that he's cut out for this kind of thing. But it's easy, so very easy to imagine Phainon here that it's almost like he is, and he can almost believe that he's capable of bringing life into this world.

"I want this."

"You don't have to make up your mind right now, my friend, you can discuss it with the other parent if that's important to you."

He slumps, placing his head in his hands. "... I cannot discuss it with him, Hyacine."

"I didn't want to assume it was him," she says quietly, carefully, as if she's afraid he'll shatter. He's heard her use that voice before on patients with grim prognoses. Perhaps she also uses it on people like him, ones teetering on the brink of the abyss, because Phainon isn't here and Mydei was never meant to do this.

A measured inhale and exhale. Another. It's difficult at first, but eventually, he forces himself to calm down.

He was never meant to do anything in his life besides fulfill the prophecy. Beyond its scope, he is his own man. He is not the crown prince Mydeimos with the expectations of thousands upon him, he is Mydei of Okhema, and he can do as he pleases.

"I want this," he repeats, with the same conviction. At the very least, he is certain of his desires, no matter how attainable they may be.

"Thank you for your patronage, lord Mydei! I hope the quality of this garment is to your liking, and if any issues arise, please bring it back. Your satisfaction is paramount."

"Of course."

The package the weaver hands to him is quite weighty, as he expected. Inside is a heavy mantle; when worn around the shoulders, it will obscure the wearer's entire form. Such a cumbersome article of clothing is not his typical style, but it is a necessity if he plans to keep his pregnancy a secret.

For now, just wearing a regular chiton instead of his revealing drape suffices to hide the slight curve of his abdomen, but it will not work for much longer. The child is growing quickly.

Perhaps all of this is more trouble than it's worth, he thinks, as he dons the mantle. Would telling the others of his condition be as difficult as wearing this dreaded thing? It likely wouldn't, but he doesn't want to chance it.

If Phainon were here, he'd know what to do--but damnit, he needs to stop thinking like that. Over the past few years, Mydei has become far too reliant on him for help. It's unbecoming.

Even though he wasn't trained in diplomacy, he's still perfectly capable of handling this matter himself. The mantle will buy him some more time to figure things out, and once he's ready, he'll--

"Hello-ooo? Mydei, are you listening?"

A loud voice interrupts his musings, and he looks down from the rooftop he's sitting upon to see the two outsiders below him. Stelle is waving as she calls his name, and Dan Heng is scowling at her.

"You have my attention now, I suppose... Do you think I look like I want to be bothered?"

"Erm, no, but this is important!"

He sighs, and then leaps down to stand at their level. Hyacine discouraged him from any intense exercise or feats of strength, but a seven meter drop is hardly an issue.

"What is so important? If it isn't a matter of life or death, I'd choose your next words carefully."

Stelle offers him a sheepish grin. "I have an invitation from Tribbie to a special party during the festival of... um, I can't remember..."

"Festival of Skirophoria," Dan Heng supplies, deadpan, and she nods eagerly.

"Yeah! It's in honor of Cerces and Phagousa!"

"I know what the festival of Skirophoria is, do you think I was born yesterday?"

"Well, you're originally from Castrum Kremnos, so I didn't know if you celebrated titans other than Nikador."

"I've lived here for years."

"Whatever, that doesn't matter. If you know so much about the festival, then you know that there's going to be a special gathering at the bathhouse! Tribbie wanted us to invite all our companions. Unfortunately, we still haven't made contact with our friends back on the Astral Express, so we've been going to everyone we know here. You're one of those people!"

"... Alright, I will come. When is it?"

He considers refusing, but he's already been reclusive enough; if he spends too much time away from the others, they'll start asking questions.

"Oh. I didn't think you'd actually accept."

"I would be a fool to reject an invitation extended by our special guests."

"Alright then! It's three weeks from today, you can show up whenever you want during the day--or night, I guess... The way you keep time here is kinda confusing, it's hard to tell what's going on when it's always bright out."

"Fortunately for you, it isn't confusing to me. I will see you at the appointed time."

Only after he has bid them farewell, walked to the market to get a meal he knows he can stomach, and then returned to his flat does he realize his error.

He just purchased this mantle to hide his body, and now he's going to go to a bathhouse to strut about in the nude? In three weeks time, his pregnancy will be obvious--Hyacine said he's carrying large.

Swearing under his breath, he unclasps the mantle, and then undoes his chiton, allowing him to turn a critical eye upon his form. His abdomen juts out in a jarring manner, entirely unmistakable when one takes in the rest of his well-muscled body. It's already obvious enough, godsdamnit.

With a weary sigh, he lays back on the bed. Exhaustion, now a familiar feeling, weighs him down. But he already knows sleep will not come to him, he has far too much on his mind.

Almost automatically, his hand comes to rest atop his swollen abdomen. Under his palm, there is life. His child. Phainon's child. What a strange concept.

Despite everything, he feels an impossible fondness. This troublesome babe will certainly grow to be a great warrior. Or, if there comes a time when Amphoreus does not need warriors, they can choose to be what they'd like. A Kremnoan would not wish for their child to be anything else, but Okhema has made him soft.

The people here are too sentimental, and it's rubbing off on him. No matter how much suffering there is in the world, their kindness shines brighter than Kephale's light. The Holy City has opened its doors to the weary masses, accepting as many as it can manage, and extending its reach to protect the rest. While the fate of the world hangs in the balance, the citizens soldier onward, not letting despair overtake them.

He can almost hear his father's voice echoing in his ears, complaining about how weak the warriors outside of Castrum Kremnos have become, and how they'll certainly fall to the Lance of Fury's devastation. Only through strife does strength blossom. There is no strength to be found in the folly of kindness.

It was the last thing he ever uttered before Mydei killed him.

Standing over his corpse, Mydei laughed at the irony as he cried for everything he'd lost. The members of the detachment watched his breakdown like an audience at a play. When he finally pulled himself together, he brushed past them out of the palace doors, head held high, not once turning back to see the devastation he'd wrought.

But that was many, many years ago. That pain is gone, and he doesn't wish to dwell on it any longer. It's already given him a headache. Groaning, he heaves himself back up; if sleep will not come to him, then he'd ought to find something to do, no matter how tired he may be.

So, he goes to Phainon's home.

It's ridiculous how much time he now spends here. He'd be more embarrassed if it didn't bring him so much comfort. He hasn't the strength to berate himself when he feels so miserable.

When he lies upon Phainon's empty bed and buries his nose into the bunched-up sheets to remind himself of his scent, it calms him. Sometimes, he uses this to go to sleep, but other times, he does more shameful things. Today is a weaker day, and so, he does the latter. His hand drifts down, finding his clit already engorged and cunt slicked--it's an excellent distraction.

He's falling apart in minutes, coming while crying Phainon's name, trembling and writhing, flesh burning hot with pleasure. But that won't be enough, he's become insatiable. His own fingers take so much work to satisfy him, and they almost don't suffice.

It reminds him far too much of his heat--all those times he spent it alone.

Before Phainon, he always hesitated to spend it with another. Mydei knows he is a difficult being to handle. He's always been violent during his heats. He bites, claws, and rips. His stamina is endless. He is unimaginably needy and controlling; whatever he desires, he will get.

Only the strongest of warriors could manage to keep up with him back in the detachment. When there was no suitable option available, he locked himself away and made do with his hands, no matter how awful he'd feel.

Phainon must be some sort of masochist for putting up with him. Mydei can only faintly recall what happens during his heats, but in the aftermath, his brutality is obvious. As a silent apology, he'll wipe Phainon's skin clean of dried blood and bandage up his lingering wounds

"I know you can't control it," he said once, after a particularly bad heat. Mydei had nearly managed to shred the collar Phainon had worn around his neck specifically to prevent a mating bite. The thick leather was in tatters, like an animal had been chewing at it.

Mydei had been rather ashamed, but hadn't mentioned it. Phainon, ever-perceptive, had noticed on his own.

"And yet, you always manage to control yourself during your rut. You've never hurt me, even though it would not damage me."

"It's because we're different people," he replied, shrugging. "Our struggles are unique. We can't help each other sort out everything, but I'm perfectly fine with doing this with you."

Oh Phainon, sweet and foolish and perfect Phainon. Mydei grinds his hips down into the mattress as he comes again, trying to make himself believe that his warm body is beneath him. The memories torment him as much as they comfort him. The familiar scent of this room is more of a taunt when he's returned to his senses.

What if this scent remains his only physical tie to Phainon? Or what if Phainon returns, but only after Mydei has given birth, and must reckon with

everything he's missed out on? Fate is cruel, perhaps to the extent that it would add onto Phainon's immense suffering.

"Please, let me see you soon," he breathes, allowing himself another moment of weakness. If the Fates hear his wish, then it will be worth it.

Chapter Notes

"You don't wish to bathe?"

Aglaea's question is innocuous on the surface. But there's more to it, because there always is with her, and it makes Mydei wince.

Of course he's not undressing, but he doesn't have a suitable excuse for why. Foolishly, he bet on the chance that nobody would press him, but certainly they'd ask. Who would come to a Skirophoria celebration and not partake in the main festivity?

Even here in the reserved section, the din from the crowded bathhouse below is audible. It seems as if the whole city has come here, more enthusiastic than ever to drink and revel in the wanton atmosphere.

If only Mydei could match their energy. In years past, he did. With enough wine in his system, he would be willing enough to share some stories from his time in the detachment, and regale onlookers with his glorious exploits. But not this time, no. He sulks off to the side, bundled in the mantle, and doesn't imbibe.

"You have to be melting under that big coat. C'mon, the water's nice and cool!"

Stelle is right, he is overheating. Even if he doesn't admit to it aloud, the sweat beading on his brow does it for him. The bathhouse isn't particularly warm, but it's humid, and with the mantle trapping his body heat, it's quite unpleasant.

Even Stelle and Dan Heng are more comfortable than him--they were initially apprehensive of the idea of public nudity, as communal bathing is

apparently not a custom of theirs, but they've adapted after the last few months in Okhema. Now, they're lounging in the water without shame.

"I'm not interested," he says vaguely.

Stelle rolls her eyes, unimpressed. "You'll accept my invitation, but won't even try to participate. I don't get it."

"It was our invitation, not just yours, and I believe that Mydei can do whatever he's comfortable with," Dan Heng replies.

"Suit yourself. I won't stop you from standing there. Anyway..."

They go back to conversing with each other about their attempts to contact their companions, leaving him alone for the time-being. Aglaea, however, seems to have no intention of letting it drop.

"Is everything alright?" she asks directly, no longer hiding behind her meandering questions.

"... It's fine."

They both know he's lying. The truth is plainly obvious. He's flapping around like a dying fish, pathetic and helpless, unable to save himself from his deficiencies. Self-deprecation does not come naturally to him; perhaps it is the hormones. It's easier to point fingers at things out of his control.

Aglaea opens her mouth to respond, then closes it. Mydei can almost see the gears churning in her head, attempting to come up with the words that will get him to confess.

All of the Chrysos Heirs have been treating him in this strange manner since Nikador's death. They're so careful, as if one misstep will cause him to lash out. And worse yet, Aglaea has only sent him on safe missions within the domain of Kephale's protection; when he protested, she spouted some nonsense excuse about not wanting to endanger his life so soon after Castrum Kremnos.

Endanger his life. Laughable, really, to try that explanation. He's not sure why he let her get away with it; he took it at face value instead of pressing for more.

It bothers him, in retrospect. Do any of them suspect that he's with child, and this is the reason for their behavior? They've already asked questions about the drastic change to his wardrobe, and his response of shrugging it off is wholly inadequate, he's already aware. They're suspicious, yes, but have they deduced the truth?

They likely haven't. Aglaea is the most discerning among them, and she still seems lost, so at the very least, he can take comfort in that fact.

"If something is the matter, I'm happy to lend my aid. Or, if you just want to talk about it, then I'll listen," she says, after a long pause. Perhaps he would appreciate the offer more if she didn't deliver it in the same detached manner as always. But her demeanor is cold despite the facsimile of warmth, and he's not encouraged to share anything at all.

"Well, I don't wish to talk about it, since it's none of your concern. It's nobody's concern but my own."

On this matter, he is steadfast. Aglaea, sensing the futility of her efforts, lays back in the bath and shuts her eyes. He's finally able to return to brooding, though in a worse mood than before.

When an attendant comes around with a tray of ornate goblets, he feels his mood foul even further. He accepts one, knowing he can't pass it up without drawing attention; the Chrysos Heirs know of his passion for good wine.

"Ooh! I didn't know we'd get drinks, this is awesome!" Stelle cries, as she takes a goblet of her own.

"Of course. This is a part of the celebration. The wine represents the cleansing waters of Phagousa, and drinking a cup will wipe away the mistakes of the previous year," Castorice explains, finally speaking up. She's been quiet since her arrival, though she's kept staring at Mydei in a way that makes his skin crawl.

"You have a lot of mistakes to cleanse," Dan Heng mutters, and Stelle elbows him hard enough to make him scowl. Mydei sometimes feels that they are kindred spirits.

"Says the dude in like three situationships at once. I've got my priorities sorted. Don't give me that look, you know I'm right."

Castorice cocks her head. "What do you mean?"

"Not important, forget I said anything. Y'know, I think we should mix up this tradition a bit... Let's make a toast! You know what that is, yeah?"

"It isn't traditional, but yes, we do have toasts," Aglaea replies. "In these circumstances, it seems appropriate. Shall we gather 'round?"

That question is mostly directed at Mydei. He wrinkles his nose in distaste, but begrudgingly walks over to the rest of the group. He'll extend this courtesy to their guests. One little sip of wine shouldn't hurt, and that will suffice for the optics. The rest can be disposed of when nobody is looking.

"Hmm, what's a good toast... 'to our good health' is boring," Stelle muses. "Maybe we can... hmm... aha! To our victories to come!"

It's quite the declaration, but there have been worse toasts, he thinks, as he clinks his chalice and then raises it to his lips.

The moment he tastes it, he remembers why he stopped drinking it weeks ago, before he even knew he was pregnant. It's become revolting. An overwhelming sourness assaults his tongue and immediately, his stomach turns as he gags into the cup. The nausea, which has lessened as of late, returns in full force.

Shit. Not now, anytime but now.

He slams the chalice down on the nearest surface out of reflex, trying to get it as far away from him as possible. The clanking noise it makes draws everyone's attention.

"Uh... Mydei? Do you not like alcohol?" Stelle asks, as she peers at him with a creased brow. "Or shit, is it poison?"

"It's not poison, I am..." he forces out, but the other words get stuck in his throat. It's quickly becoming obvious to him that the nausea will not pass on its own, no matter how hard he tries to repress it. He's going to be sick.

With a hand clasped over his mouth, he strides away, ignoring the calls of his name behind him. Each step brings the inevitable closer. He feels like he can't walk straight. Through some miraculous effort, he makes it out of earshot and into a deserted corridor, where he sinks to his knees and vomits into a potted plant.

His stomach doesn't settle until his throat is raw and his eyes sting from exertion. Somehow, the foul tang of bile in his mouth isn't as unpleasant as the wine. His favorite drink has been ruined--yet another sacrifice made for this child.

He hangs his head down, groaning softly. How utterly embarrassing this all has been. At this point, there is no way he can return to the gathering; it seems he'll be heading home early.

How lovely would it be to go rest at Phainon's house, but he doesn't think he can stand making the walk there. He doesn't want to spend another moment in public longer than is necessary. Never has it been such a relief to step into the dim, scarcely-furnished flat he otherwise detests.

He manages to make it into the bedroom before there is a knock at the door. Of course somebody followed him.

"Lord Mydei, please let me in," Castorice's muffled voice calls, after he doesn't respond.

"I'm not accepting visitors right now," he shouts back, not bothering to police the hostility in his tone.

"It is an order from Aglaea, I must check on you. I will break down the door if necessary."

Not wanting to deal with the hassle, he opens the door. Castorice, waiting at the doorstep, immediately takes a few steps back, distancing herself from him.

"Okay, you've checked on me. I'm alive. Now go."

She takes a measured breath, as if preparing herself. "I know the truth."

"What?"

"I know about the babe within you."

"Fuck."

All of the tension leaves his body in an instant, and his knees almost buckle beneath him. So, this is it: the revelation. It feels worse than he imagined it would. With the last of his remaining energy, he stumbles to the small dining room and collapses in one of the chairs.

Castorice follows, taking the seat across from him. She doesn't say anything, she only looks at him expectantly, as if he's meant to say something.

"How long have you known?" he finally decides to ask, voice hoarse.

"I've sensed the abundance of life force within you for months. It was quite weak at first, and I only figured out the source in the Vortex of Genesis when you became ill. But you obviously didn't know, and I did not feel it was appropriate for me to inform you of the news."

"And when did the others find out? Just now?"

"Oh, they still don't know."

"What?"

That should be a relief, but it's more of a shock. It seems impossible. "Were they not paying attention to a thing that happened? I feel it's easy to deduce the reason for my behavior."

"They believe you to be heartbroken over Lord Phainon."

"... Aglaea would assume that, yes, but even the outsiders?"

"Stelle said that you 'made it so painfully obvious' and she felt uncomfortable being with you in Castrum Kremnos because you were 'basically fucking right in'--"

"That's enough, I've heard enough chatter from that insufferable outsider," he grits out. "I didn't think it was that apparent, godsdamnit."

"It wasn't so apparent to me, I only guessed after learning of your pregnancy. I know that isn't much of a comfort, since I am not particularly adept at understanding social interactions. In any case, they do not seem to have suspicions of any other issues ailing you."

He sighs heavily. "That is some comfort, I suppose."

"Why are you so concerned about them finding out?"

"I believe Aglaea would be displeased, to put it lightly... I'd rather not take the risk. This is a calculated decision on my part, and I've already thought it through. At least until Phainon returns, I will not inform anybody. That is final."

They both know that his resolve is somewhat flawed in nature, but she nods in affirmation anyway, and offers him the closest thing to a smile that she can muster.

"I understand. If you wish for it to remain a secret, then I shall keep it too, Lord Mydei."

"... Many thanks, Castorice," he mumbles, the gratitude as stilted and awkward as always, though he means it genuinely.

"And if you'd like my aid, I can try to do what you require, though I'm not sure it will be adequate. I believe it is the thought that counts, yes? Loneliness is a terrible pain to bear. That, at least, I hope to ease."

He's poised to brush off her offer, but can't bring himself to refuse, not in these circumstances. Is he lonely? Yes. Desperately so. Without Phainon, it's as if a part of him is hollowed out. He was a pure shining light to match the ferocity of Mydei's fire, gentleness juxtaposed with rough edges, a practiced blade against raw, wild power.

Does Phainon feel his absence as profoundly, wherever he may be? Does he look to the sky and imagine them reunited, and whisper his hopes for the Fates to hear?

By the gods, Mydei has become so sickeningly sentimental. This man has ruined him.

"Would you like for me to leave now?" Castorice asks, bringing him out of his reprieve. "I can inform the others that you are in a bad mood, and that you will not be returning to the celebration."

"That will suffice, yes--"

He's interrupted by a deafening crash, so loud that the sound seems to rattle around inside his skull and grate against his brain. In the aftermath, there's pandemonium; metal squeals against metal, people scream, and alarms begin to blare, though he can barely hear it over the ringing in his ears.

Most notable to him, however, is the low rumble that seems to shake the room. It's the chanting of Titankin, distant but overwhelming. He'd recognize it anywhere; it resonates with his very being, commanding his attention. And though he cannot understand the language of titans, he can easily glean the meaning of their cries.

It seems the Titankin, now masterless, still thirst for blood.

In an instant, he's shot to his feet, fists readied and gauntlets materialized. Around him, the air hums with energy; the power of Fury bows to him like a loyal subject, ready to do his bidding.

"The invading force is large, the guards will need our support," he says, already making his way to the door.

Castorice has summoned her scythe, but she hesitates to follow him. "Are you certain you should be placing yourself in danger--"

"The child will be alright."

"But nurturing life within you takes energy, will you have the strength for a difficult battle?"

"I have to have the strength, it is my duty."

"... If you're certain."

She doesn't protest anymore, and the two of them rush into the fray side by side.

The Titankin have attempted many, many times, to breach the walls of the Holy City. They are as unrelenting as the tide, no matter how many failures they suffer and how thin their ranks become. Their corpses litter the hills, have piled up in drifts from the sheer number, and yet, they march on.

It is rare that they succeed in making it past the gates, but it has happened. On one such occasion, they managed to launch a projectile at the walls, destroying a portion of it and allowing them entry in a place that wasn't well-guarded.

Today, it seems they are trying that approach again.

Mydei leaps through the breach to find a squadron of Titankin just meters away; if he had been a few seconds late, he would've found himself in the midst of disaster. Behind him is a tightly-packed district of civilian homes. Crisis still isn't averted; at any point, they could make it through, and the carnage would be unfathomable.

Castorice went to the front gates, but perhaps she should've come here to lend her aid. As it is, there isn't time for him to plan through his attack. He lunges at the nearest warrior, fist connecting with such force that it's thrown back into its comrades behind it, disintegrating them as well. He then falls

into a roll, dodging a volley of arrows launched at his head. The archers are usually his main priority, but now, it's the praetor shambling forward, greatsword drawn and alight with golden fire.

He effortlessly constructs a greatsword of his own, blood flowing into his palm to crystalize into a blade to block the strike. The force of the praetor's downswing is devastating, enough to fell any ordinary mortal, but Mydei, of course, is unyielding. His opponent staggers back, guard lowered, affording him the opportunity to cleave its head in twain.

Now he can take care of the pesky archers. They shoot another volley; he easily sidesteps, then beheads them each with brutal, forceful swings.

"Good work, lil' De!" Tribbie cheers, and he whips around to find her fluttering at the ruined wall. Her two sisters are lost in prayer beside her, slowly molding the stone back into place.

"How long until the breach is repaired?"

She glances at her sisters, then back at him. "Probably a while, the damage is severe. You'll hold the baddies off until then?"

"Of course," he answers, unable to stop himself from grinning. Another squadron is approaching, and it's time for him to lose himself in the heat of battle.

Oh, how he's missed this, he thinks, as he charges forward. Titankin topple like paper dolls, stone bodies cracking under the might of his fists and blood. They attempt to attack--every swing misses. He's a blur of destruction, alight with the thrill that he's been deprived of for far too long.

This is what he was born to do.

Another praetor charges forward, and he vaults over its blade, causing it to stumble. It's pathetic how it doesn't even try to stop him as he forms a lance to drive straight through its body. Its ichor sprays across his exposed skin, painting him with liquid gold. The rest soaks into the mantle. His smile sharpens. His chest burns with exhilaration.

When he fights, he uses a weapon until he tires of it; boredom has no place on the battlefield. His greatsword is lobbed at the first thing he sees move, and he proceeds forth with the lance, impaling and gutting with glee. Marble punctures as easily as fabric when he's the one attacking. He's an unstoppable force.

Even the fiercest of Kremnoan warriors would not participate in such debauched combat, not like him. They'd have caution, would think before acting to avoid injury. Mydei doesn't think of anything beyond what he can see around him. There's no need for strategy. Any pain he experiences is fuel for the fire within him, coaxing it to grow stronger, to turn into something so terrible that it nearly consumes him, too.

Aglaea once said that he will melt himself down one day. She's probably right, and he doesn't care. If he cared, then he would not be fit for his role in the prophecy. To the undying, all things are temporary.

A wily archer shoots at him while he's removing his lance from his latest target, and the arrow connects, piercing the meat of his shoulder. Finally, an opponent with some wit. He laughs at the pain as he rips it from his flesh. Then, he hurls his lance at the archer's face with pinpoint accuracy, obliterating its skull. A moment later and the wound has sealed itself shut, fibers of muscle weaving back into place.

Wave after wave of Titankin descend upon him, and each one fails to overwhelm him. He cycles through weapons at random, stabbing and bludgeoning and whipping, until he loses the patience for such dignity, and then uses raw bursts of crystalized blood, shredding through everything that dares to approach.

The real challenge has yet to come, though he's readying himself for its arrival: a hulking colossus, slow-moving but deadly, a hundred-odd meters tall and strong enough to destroy anything in its path. Its weak point is at the base of its skull, where the stone is thinnest. He always relishes the struggle of the climb when he has the opportunity to fight this variety of Titankin.

As he makes his way towards it, he finds that he has company: Stelle, approaching from the opposite direction. She's holding her own, of course, but regardless of her skill, it's a troubling sight.

He starts to run, tearing past Titankin quicker than they can react.

"Outsider!" he shouts the moment he's within earshot. "What are you doing?"

"Fighting, of course!" Stelle yells back, before whacking a Titankin in the head with her baseball bat, causing it to collapse in a heap.

He falls into step alongside her. "There is no need to endanger yourself, the Chrysos Heirs have this under control. Get back to the city."

"We're not in any danger right now, Dan Heng is in his Vidyadhara form, he's gonna--" she pauses to cave a warrior's chest in, "--kill everything in sight, no problem. And you guys looked like you didn't have everything under control. I mean, you were just off moping about Phainon, yeah?"

"I was not moping," he growls, "and I would rather you not be out here, even if you insist it's fine. We shouldn't take any unnecessary risks."

"Dude, if monsters get into the city we'll be at way more of a risk. I'd rather go do shit than twiddle my thumbs waiting to die."

"Do not call me... ugh, never mind. At the very least, allow me to handle the colossus, and keep your distance from it."

"As long as you let us keep fighting, I guess it's fine... Okay! I'll go bother Dan Heng!"

She prances off, swinging at nearby Titankin with reckless abandon. Once he's satisfied with the distance between them, he turns his attention to the colossus, now looming in his periphery.

It raises a foot, prepared to squash him, and he dashes to its other leg, where he begins the treacherous climb to its neck. The chinks in its armor act as handholds in some places, but in others, he creates picks to jam into the

stone, allowing him to pull himself up with his upper body, his feet braced uselessly against smooth marble.

It is immensely difficult. His muscles scream in protest after only a few minutes. And the colossus, aware of his presence, keeps trying to shake him off, forcing him to pause, clinging desperately to the picks until it stills, lest he get tossed to the ground. He's not keen on making this climb a second time.

Once he's made it up to its hips, there's a ledge big enough for him to stand on, and he pauses for a moment to catch his breath. As he hoped, the colossus now tries to swat at him; it's easy enough to make the jump to its hand.

As quickly as he can manage, he clambers up the forearm. He's in a vulnerable position now, as the colossus has an excellent view of anything he does. Its other hand attempts to grab him, but its fine motor skills are lacking, and it completely misses, granting him a few extra seconds to run. He leaps over the elbow joint to begin the final climb up its bicep. It's steep, and the going is slow. Behind him, he can hear the fingers readjusting--with a final burst of effort, he throws himself forward, just narrowly avoiding its pincer grip.

Finally, he's made it to safety atop the shoulders. Chest heaving from exertion, he stumbles to its neck, eyes trained upward at the base of the skull. Already, he's discarded the picks for a heavy javelin, one suitable for the final blow.

It's a difficult throw to manage. The angle is poor and the wind is blowing hard at this elevation. But Mydei does not miss. His aim is true, and the javelin rams into the weak spot, shattering the rock and causing ichor to cascade out.

The colossus tilts dangerously to the side, nearly causing him to lose his fitting. It's already weak; in less than a minute, it will completely fall apart. He'd rather not be on it when that happens.

So, he jumps.

For any ordinary person, this would be a fatal move. For him, it is an unpleasant landing, but his body distributes the force, and he's back on his feet in an instant, ready to parry a strike from a Titankin, and kick another away. After dispatching them both, he's free to watch the result of his handiwork.

The dying colossus has sunk to its knees, and with a mighty groan, it slumps forward, slamming into the ground and shattering into a thousand pieces. Titankin are crushed by its heavy corpse, others toppled by the shockwave of its fall. Ichor splatters across the battlefield.

"Excellent," he says to himself, before returning to combat. There's no time to rest on his laurels.

But something is wrong.

The Titankin swarm around him, the killer of their mighty colossus--that's not the issue, no, he should be able to handle them. This is no different than anything else that's happened in this battle. And yet, his body is no longer responding as he expects. Exhaustion pulls at his limbs, worsening by the minute. He desperately forces himself to continue, but he only manages to fell a few more Titankin before his strikes are too sluggish and weak to even damage them.

He's suddenly on the defensive, gauntlets raised to block, not punch, as he scrambles to pull himself together--to no avail. His legs are trembling. The edges of his vision have vignetted. His skull feels like it's been stuffed with cloth.

But nurturing life within you takes energy, will you have the strength for a difficult battle?

Damnit, why is Castorice always right?

He knows he can't keep press on, not like this, but he's surrounded on all sides, and the only way out is to fight. He whips around, searching for a gap to retreat through. There's nothing. He's trapped, helpless in the face of his enemies.

In the throng of approaching Titankin, an archer raises its longbow. An arrow is notched, and the bowstring is drawn back. He orders his body to move out of the way. It should be easy, so easy to dodge.

But instead, when the arrow flies, it finds its mark in his chest.

Immediately, pain erupts within him as the air is ejected from his lung in a strangled gasp. He feels his left lung folding on itself--it's punctured. The arrow slipped through his rib cage and buried itself underneath his heart.

He collapses. His head cracks against the hard ground. His brain slams against the inside of his skull and sparks explode in his vision. It takes all his willpower to not vomit; lying prone as he is, he'd choke.

However painful they may be, an arrow wound and a concussion are trivial injuries. He should be able to get up and continue fighting. He's managed to win battles with most of his guts hanging out of his abdominal cavity, this is nothing.

Come on, get up.

He can't move. Everything is going dark, and he's suddenly cold, despite how rapidly his heart is pounding. It blankets him, urging him to just close his eyes and drift away from it all--his consciousness is a fragile thing, just barely maintained.

It's a familiar sensation, though it's been a very long time since his last true death. He is so skilled, and his healing is so rapid that it's rare for his heart to get to a point where it stops.

To be an undying mortal does not mean that he doesn't die--he does. It just comes with a caveat. His soul is so tightly bound to his flesh that it cannot leave at the cessation of his heartbeat. Death attempts to embrace him, but its reach does not extend through the barrier of his skin.

Once his body has regenerated enough to sustain life, his consciousness returns, and he is able to rise again. It isn't a pleasant process--far from it, really--but it's a quick one, no matter how brutally he is maimed.

In these low stakes, he didn't anticipate a death. It's always fine, no more significant than any other injury in its impermanence--but this time is different, isn't it? This time, there's another life he must consider beyond his own. The child within him seems to possess some of his undying qualities, but to what extent, he doesn't know. It is possible that it may not survive a lack of blood flow while his heart attempts to restart itself.

To think that an unimportant battle like this could be the thing that kills it-- what a twisted sense of humor Fate has. After all this child has weathered, it is only now, after he's learned of its existence, that it dies.

He manages to move, just enough to limply place his hand upon the swell of his abdomen. It is a futile act of protection. Dear gods above, he doesn't want to lose it, and yet, he is powerless to stop the Titankin from marching forth.

He resists unconsciousness with the last bit of energy remaining within him, refusing to let his eyes close; he glares up in defiance at the warrior looming above him. At the very least, he will not cower before his killer. It raises its blade above his heart. He braces himself for the agony of death.

But the pain never comes.

Instead, a great blast of concentrated water vaporizes the Titankin, and all of the others in the vicinity.

Perhaps he is hallucinating, but he swears he sees the outsider Dan Heng hovering above him, head now crowned with a set of horns, commanding the water to tear through the enemy ranks. His power is magnificent; it takes the form of a majestic beast, then shifts into spears to rain down devastation, and then a vortex, crushing stone bodies into heaps of ichor-soaked rumble.

"Go check on Mydei, I've got the rest under control!" he hears Stelle say, voice seeming to come from a thousand miles away.

In an instant, Dan Heng is kneeling beside him. "Mydei, are you conscious?"

He tries to respond, but his breath catches as he inhales, and he begins to cough, blood spilling from his lips. It doesn't seem to end--so much has pooled in his lung and with the arrow still lodged within, the wound is unable to begin healing.

He's bleeding to death internally, he knows. His body can only regenerate his blood so quickly, and with the child sapping his energy, that limit has been reached.

"Don't waste your breath," Dan Heng urges, eyes widening in the most outward display of panic Mydei has seen from him. "I am going to use my magic to heal your wound, it may feel strange. Prepare yourself."

No, he wishes to protest, just remove the arrow, my body will do the rest. But the only noise he produces is a groan, thick with the blood caught in his throat.

Dan Heng positions his hands on his chest, and something within Mydei responds, surging to meet Dan Heng's touch. It feels intrusive more than anything else.

"Do you feel that? Focus on it, on that sensation."

For a moment, nothing seems to happen, until Dan Heng murmurs a chant. Mydei seizes from the pure, shining bolt of agony that tears through him. It hurts in a way that he's never experienced before. It's like his blood has turned to magma, burning him from the inside out, in every inch of his body. Involuntarily, he tries to scream, and coughs wetly instead, each one gurgling as blood gushes into his lung. His mouth is coated in the taste of iron.

It's intolerable. He can't do this, he can't take it, it's too foreign, too terrible, and his entire world is reduced to it, this pain ripping his insides into pieces. His body contorts--the hurt is inescapable, it only gets worse.

This isn't healing him, it's killing him.

"Shit!" Dan Heng recoils suddenly, his composure breaking. Sweat rolls down his face as he gasps for air. "That wasn't... Your body isn't compatible with my abilities. We need an actual doctor from the city who can take care of you."

"No," Mydei finally manages to say, his voice a ragged mess.

"You need medical attention. You'll certainly--no, you're immortal, of course. My apologies. But if you're immortal, why has this injury..."

Dan Heng trails off; after a moment of pause, he draws his spear and makes a quick cut through the fabric of the mantle, allowing him to see the truth that Mydei has concealed for all these weeks.

It clearly wasn't what he expected to find. The severity of his injury is now obvious, but so is his pregnancy. Hesitantly, Dan Heng reaches a hand towards his abdomen, and then, thinking twice, pulls back.

"Stelle, we need to get Mydei to the city. It's urgent."

"Why, isn't he immortal? He'll get better on his own--"

"He's pregnant, and I'm not sure what else to do."

"What? Oh fuck, okay, umm... I'll clear a path, give me a few minutes!"

Dan Heng looks back at him. "I'm going to carry you. Is that alright?"

"... Remove ... arrow..." he heaves, each word a monumental effort. He'll die long before they reach the city if his body isn't able to begin healing.

"Remove the arrow? I can try."

Dan Heng grabs the shaft, clearly uncertain on how to proceed. He's no medic, not in the traditional sense. Whatever ability he tried to use earlier must've been the extent of his healing prowess. He leans in to inspect the wound, a frown tugging at his mouth. Then, without any warning, he yanks hard--the arrowhead slides from Mydei's lung, but catches on the inside of his rib cage, preventing its removal.

Not good.

His flesh, mistakenly believing that it's appropriate to begin healing, rapidly closes around the foreign body. Now instead of piercing his lung, the arrow has become a part of it. He feels the fibers of muscle and tissue snag on the metal--they can't properly seal the tear, and blood continues to drip into his lung with every contraction of his heart.

Dan Heng tries again, but this time, the arrow doesn't budge.

"Stop, it's... healed into my body, Hyacine will... surgically remove it," he pants, finally able to speak again. Some healing is better than nothing.

"Hyacine is a doctor?"

"Yes, she's a Chrysos Heir, she'll know... what to do..."

He tries to stand, but his body is still too weak, and he can't even manage to get to his knees. Dan Heng hefts him up in a bridal carry, the torn remnants of his mantle left on the ground. He doesn't protest the loss. It was foolish of him to believe this was ever something he could hide indefinitely. For better or for worse, the others will find out, and he will weather the consequences.

"... Mydei said to find you, apparently the arrow has healed into his body."

"Oh, hello new friends! Dannie, Grayie, I've heard so much about you! But we'll get properly introduced later. Put him down on this cot, I can take care of him. Do you two have any injuries?"

"Umm... No, we're both unharmed. We're needed on the battlefield, is it alright if we leave?"

"Fret not, your companion is in good hands here. Stay safe!"

Mydei drifts back into consciousness as he's laid down in Hyacine's infirmary. His mind is working sluggishly--seems the concussion hasn't

quite resolved.

"I'm acting as your doctor right now," Hyacine begins, "so I won't berate you, but... I advised you against strenuous activity, and you decided to run into battle with no regard for your safety. You need to take better care of yourself right now, my friend."

"I had to help. How many casualties would there have been without my intervention?" he rasps. A metallic taste still lingers on his tongue.

"It's not about that, it's... Never mind. This arrow has to be cut out."

For him, surgery is not a delicate process. After he's stuffed a rag into his mouth to bite down on, Hyacine begins the procedure, using a scalpel to slice through the freshly-healed tissue around the arrow, and in one swift movement, finally extracts it.

It took a series of long arguments to convince her to disregard standard medical protocol when treating him. In these dire times, supplies are hard to come by, and it would be a waste to use them on somebody who won't reap the benefits. He doesn't need painkillers or blood transfusions. Hyacine doesn't need to waste her valuable time on careful incisions when his body will mend regardless of what she does.

When Phainon would accompany him here in the past, he'd insist on painkillers. With those pleading eyes of his, he'd bend Mydei's resolve with ease, and he'd accept the injection, even though it barely worked. But now, Phainon isn't here, and this pain is borne alone.

Funny how the little things he once found so annoying have become the things he misses so deeply.

In just a few minutes, his wound has completely closed over, the only indication that it was ever there being a faint scar that will inevitably fade within the next day.

No matter what Hyacine tells him, he can't disregard his duties for his own sake. He needs to return to battle; of course, he'll stay away from the front

lines. There is certainly more to be done elsewhere. Guarding the Tribios as they finish their repairs should suffice.

But as he's clambering out of the cot while her back is turned, somebody enters the infirmary, and he stills.

"How many casualties so far?" he hears Aglaea asks.

"Twenty-two, none of them are fatalities."

"Thank the titans you're still in Okhema, I'm certain that there may have been some fatalities without your expertise. How many of the injured are you tending to here?"

"Oh, you flatter me! I have fifteen of the most serious ones, the others I directed to the general hospital. All are in stable condition. One is technically ready for discharge."

"Ready so soon? Is it..."

Footsteps rapidly approach his cot, and Aglaea peers around the curtain, locking eyes with him.

"Mydei."

He can only stand to hold her gaze for a moment before he looks down in shame.

"Lady Aglaea," he mutters, as if the honorific will temper her ire.

It's quiet, too quiet. There is too much to say, and he can't hope to explain himself, not now, not after all that has transpired.

"If I'm not mistaken, you are with child, yes?" Her tone, as always, is unreadable. He nods, knowing that any lie would be meaningless.

"I thought I had detected a change in your scent, but I attributed it to your sadness over Phainon, I didn't consider that you may be afflicted with more than a broken heart. My apologies."

He turns to her again, finding her expression passive, not twisted in anger as he expected. "Why do you apologize?"

"You believed you had a reason to hide this from us, and had to suffer alone."

"Does this not interfere with your plans? I've become a liability." It pains him to say, but it is the truth. His performance on the battlefield was evidence enough.

"You've always been a part of the prophecy. If this was an issue, your fate would not be decreed by its words. I understand your hesitation, but I assure you, I hold no contempt--you are free to do as you wish. Entanglement of the romantic variety between the Chrysos Heirs is not unheard of, and has not caused significant tension in the past."

"Phainon and I are not... in that variety of relationship."

Aglaea smiles, a trace hint of mischief within it. "I hold the Coreflame of the romance titan, it has always been obvious to me what you felt for each other, even if you did not admit to it."

"Of course," he sighs. The revelation is not as terrible as he imagined; in fact, it feels as if a great weight has been lifted from his shoulders. What a relief to not have to worry about this nonsense anymore.

"All of this is to say," Aglaea continues, "that you do not have to hide from us any longer. I, and the other Chrysos Heirs, will offer our support. That is my sincere promise. Now, please get some rest. I know you wish to return to combat, but that will be unnecessary. You've already done enough, and the invading force has nearly been defeated. The city guards can handle the remaining Titankin."

"If you're certain."

"I am. The breach has been repaired, and the main gates--"

Again, the door to the infirmary is opened, though this time with so much force that it slams into the wall. Tribbie rockets over, frantic. Mydei's heart sinks to his feet.

"Come to the Vortex of Genesis quickly! Snowy is in trouble!"
