Chapter Notes

There is no word for fear in the Kremonan language.

That does not mean Kremnoans do not know fear, they simply choose not to speak of it. Even Mydei has fears--they are not plentiful in number, but they exist, whether he acknowledges them or not.

Now, his greatest fear is being realized.

The Vortex of Genesis is quiet and empty, except for one soul--and that soul is not Phainon. Trinnon stands at the altar, her hands clenched together against her chest, visibly shaking. Mydei feels sick.

"I can't hear Snowy's voice anymore..." she says, distraught, "something is burning him up inside the trial... His soul is turning to ash."

He didn't want it to come to this, but now, only one choice remains. If it means saving Phainon, he will sacrifice himself in a heartbeat. He can only pray that this sacrifice will not bring down his forsaken people alongside him.

"Get ready, Mydeimos." Aglaea's voice is solemn. They spoke of this fail-safe plan in advance, before Phainon even began the trial, but he hoped, so deeply, that it would not be enacted. She knows of this hope, and perhaps knew it was misguided this entire time.

Phainon was never going to be able to seize Nikador's Coreflame, of course not. It is not for him to bear.

Mydei inhales deeply, trying to banish the tightness in the back of his throat. "I will intervene as promised, and I will bring him to safety. I will do no more."

What a fool he is to hesitate on the edge of this great precipice, and yet, he still lacks the courage to make this leap, no matter how necessary it may be.

Nobody else could ever attempt to preside over the power of strife but Mydeimos. The Coreflame will be his, sooner or later. He can run from it now, but it is a chase he is fated to lose. Destiny is breathing down the back of his neck, waiting to crown him as the next king of Kremnos.

For now, Aglaea doesn't press him. "Certainly. This is not the time to make any more demands of you."

"Wait, is it really okay for Mydei to participate in the trial when he's, you know, in such a delicate condition?" Stelle interrupts. He's poised to interject, but Aglaea beats him to it.

"The trial is not a physical thing, it involves only the mind and soul. The babe within Mydei's body will come to no harm, so long as the strength of his will is sound, but if it would settle your worries, you may accompany him in the retrieval mission."

"Their help would be appreciated at this moment--the trial is more challenging than anything I have faced before. There is no telling what we may encounter in a realm born from strife incarnate."

Castorice looks to the outsiders, frowning. "And perhaps that is why they should not accompany you. Our distinguished guests should not risk the safety of their souls, this is not their duty. Allow me to go with you instead."

"No," he replies firmly. "Someone must stay outside in case we also need to be extracted."

"If Phainon's life is on the line, as Nameless, we're poised to do what is necessary, even if it is risky," Dan Heng affirms, and Stelle nods eagerly, while offering a reassuring grin.

"We can handle it, don't worry!"

"Then you two shall join me. We'll locate Phainon, and once he is found, Aglaea's golden thread will guide us to freedom, so long as we are able to withstand Nikador's wrath. If the worst does happen, then Castorice, you will be the one to rescue the outsiders. I can find my own way out."

Of that, he is certain. This trial was made for him, and he can bend the power of fury to his will, enough to escape.

"Now, steel your resolve, and keep close within your heart the memories of valor you possess. Your strength will be the only thing you can rely on, besides me. Follow my lead."

There is no word for fear in the Kremonan language.

But long ago, Mydei had many fears. Each night, gathered around the fire with his closest comrades, he feared that those may be the last hours they were able to spend with each other before the specter of death found them. Perdikkas, Leonnius, Ptolemy, Hephaestion, Peucesta--those five men grew up alongside him into fine warriors, but it was always certain that they would die before him. The thought haunted him just as it infuriated him.

It was weak-minded of him, he knew, and no honorable Kremnoan would have such worries. His friends did not fear death, certainly not--they threw themselves into battle alongside him, matching his bravery without the shield of an undying body. And yet, no matter how many times he told himself that it would not break him, it did.

Each time one fell, he struggled more and more to keep the pain bottled up inside. He was the leader of the detachment, he couldn't grieve for warriors who had, by all accounts, died glorious deaths. But he grieved anyway. Behind closed doors, he wept bitterly over what possessions they could recover from the battlefield. Perdikkas's book of remedies, pages soaked in his own blood; Peucesta's golden lyre, strings snapped; Ptolemy's lance, broken in half; poor Leonnius's death was so brutal they couldn't even find his body, and Mydei had naught but his memories.

It would never be enough. Their lives meant something more than what they left behind. Why should he not mourn?

That is when the seeds of doubt were first sown. To see death so intimately, as an untouchable spectator, was to see how pointless it really was. Each death rattle that passed the lips of a friend was a needless sacrifice. Each grave dug in haste was a pointless honor.

Is there really any glory in death?

The day Mydei killed his father, his dear Hephaestion died too, and he finally broke. When he managed to piece himself back together, his heart had crystalized into something hard and unfeeling. Perhaps there is no glory in death, but there will be no sadness, he told himself. The crown prince had no need for tears.

He thought he'd well and truly left the past behind him. How strange is it, then, to find himself faced with a man donning the visage of a ghost.

"Tell me your name, brute! Your demise shall be a tale I boast of at the victory feast!"

"My name... is Perdikkas, and I am here... to avenge my people."

The passage of time has dulled his memories, but that face, and that resolute voice, will never leave his mind. He would not deign to forget one of his dearest friends. This man laid with him during his heats to temper them, no matter how violent. Perdikkas was strong yet gentle, loyal to no end, and a beacon of stability they all could rely upon when the world itself seemed to oppose them.

"Do you feel any shame when staying with me in estrus?" he'd asked one night while the others were out hunting. He was polishing his gauntlets, and Perdikkas was brewing up another batch of antibiotics to treat the wounded.

"Why should I?"

"I am the first omega to come from my lineage... Am I not a stain upon Kremnos?" It is a moment of vulnerability that he would look back on with some shame in the coming weeks, but he could no longer act as if his secondary sex did not bother him.

"You did not choose the circumstances of your birth, but you have proven yourself to be the strongest warrior in all the lands, so I don't think it matters. Omega, alpha, or beta--we are all humans with the ability of choice. It is only a hindrance if you allow it to be. In my eyes, you're a great prince. I certainly don't care what may lie between your legs."

"I suppose that is true. I just don't wish to disappoint the detachment if they learn what I am."

"If they're disappointed in you, then they are fools undeserving of a place in your army. We've all seen you fight, Mydei. Even the most close-minded idiot cannot deny your skill."

"... Thank you, Perdikkas," he'd said softly, and then, gone back to working in silence, as if no conversation had transpired.

They never spoke of that matter again, but those words did not leave Mydei's mind. It was with Perdikkas's help that he unlearned the shame he held for his body. That man shaped his perspective on life, and what did Mydei offer in return? Nothing, for he did not have the chance.

Even now, with this ghost before him, Mydei can only watch.

The Okheman warrior threatening Perdikkas laughs, and draws his xiphos closer to his face. "Perdikkas? Even the tragic cries of beasts at the slaughterhouse make prettier noises than your name!"

It takes all of Mydei's strength to hold himself back. How easy it would be to launch himself at this stupid warrior and reduce his body to bloody pulp-- but none of this is real. Perdikkas is dead, he never made it to Okhema, he never even made it to stand by him as he slew his father. The trial is just trying to play with him.

"Say whatever you'd like... despicable wretch. It is always better... to die in glory than to return... even in victory. May the Kremnoan spirit always run within me!"

"I see you're eager to die and join your comrades in the hells! Very well then, I shall grant that wish!"

Mydei does not intervene as Perdikkas's throat is slit in one clumsy slash. He does not wince as Perdikkas gurgles, throat filled with blood. He does not move to catch Perdikkas as he falls to the ground.

"Avenge... me..."

Even those words, said with the voice of his friend, do not force him to act. Resolute, he watches the warrior chuckle to himself, before he turns to face them.

"Oh, I see another Kremnoan brute has a death wish--and it's the alpha! The pathetic, cowardly king himself."

The alpha, hilarious. He supposes he looks the part right now, as his body shows no sign of pregnancy, not here in this domain of the spirit. He is unburdened by the weight of a child in his womb. And what a heavy burden it is.

What a disappointment he must have been to his father, what anger must he have felt when he looked upon the face of his newborn son. This weak male omega was prophesied to set Castrum Kremnos aflame--how could it be true? The Fates must have been mistaken in their soothsaying.

They were not mistaken, of course. Mydei believes he has proven himself enough. Indeed, secondary sex has no bearing on strength, or lack thereof.

"A true coward would slit the throat of a dying man who cannot even muster the strength to defend themself. Where is your shame, haikas?"

The warrior grins cruelly. "You dogs do not deserve honorable deaths. I'll give you what you deserve."

Mydei sneers, readying his fists. When the form of the warrior warps, becoming a crumbling Titankin, he cannot resist the urge to shred its body into dust. In an instant, there is nothing left but rock and crystalized blood spiked in the ground. He hoped it would appease his anger, yet the chanting that echoes in his head does not quiet. His brain feels as if it's pushing out of his skull.

"This insatiable bloodlust... It could only be a product of Nikador's wrath. I've seen this Okheman before. Strife contorted an honorable warrior into a perverse beast."

"It's getting to me too," Stelle mumbles, as she places her hand against her forehead. "It feels like I've had one too many soulglads to drink... ugh. We need to find Dan Heng quick."

"Certainly. It can destroy the wits of even the bravest warriors--it got to Phainon, that's why he lost himself, the fool."

Stelle appraises him for a moment, and then glances to Perdikkas's corpse, still leaking blood on the ruined cobblestones. "You seemed upset earlier, did you know this guy or something?"

"... It's nothing. Let's go."

It is a relief to proceed onward once they reunite with Dan Heng. The sooner they can locate Phainon and leave this place, the better. Resisting the fury surging within him is becoming more difficult by the minute. It is a siren song, drawing him toward their destination: the true entrance to the trial.

Nikador themself is the one manipulating this trial. He had his suspicions, but seeing their incarnation standing before him, there is no doubt.

"Ah, Mydeimos. Thou art a keen warrior, indeed. I would expect no less from the blasphemous prince of Castrum Kremnos."

His god's voice rings in his ears, overpowering the sounds of battle around them. Mydei braces himself against it, to no avail. This is not that madness-

drunk beast he fought in his birthplace, no, this is Nikador's true self. To stand before them is akin to standing in front of the sun itself, so intense is the heat of their fury. He fears it may just drive him insane.

"Thou art here for the soul of thy lover, yes?"

He wrinkles his nose in distaste. How is even Nikador aware of their entanglement? Perhaps it is easier to tell here, in this domain of pure thought and emotion, what he harbors for this man.

"I am. Hand over that poor excuse for a swordmaster, and let's be done with this farce."

The incarnation huffs, crossing their arms against their chest. "I applaud thy courage, but as impressive as it is, I cannot turn a blind eye as thou besmirch the dignity of one who has fallen.

"He faced the greatest fear in the depths of his heart and fought with exceptional valor, but he eventually succumbed to the brutal onslaught. I whisked him off to the rear battleground, and granted him glory worthy of his tenacity and sacrifice. If thou wish to take him away, thou must prove that thy resolve is a rival to his own."

"Do you think I fear bloodshed? Show me your worst, mad king, and I shall prove myself against it. If I must slay you again, so be it. The Deliverer's return is imminent."

"Commendable! Few forces have such potency as mortal love. Thy noble mother displayed the same spirit with a spear in her hands."

"Do not speak of her," he growls. They're just riling him up, he knows, but he cannot cling to his last bit of sanity any longer. If this is where he loses himself, then it will be acceptable. To bring back Phainon, he must fight with an intensity he has not reached before. Anger may be the kindling he needs to reach his apex.

When his mother died, he was not even a year old--he hasn't a single memory of her. Even so, he mourns her--mourns the life he could have

lived were his father not ruined by selfish visions of divinity. The pain of her loss, and its senseless nature, has always enraged him.

Yes, his father may have been the one to pierce her heart, but something else guided his hand that was not his own resolve.

"Why not? She challenged the dishonorable king to a duel, knowing it was a trap, all to protect thy dignity. Art thou suggesting all her efforts were for naught?"

"It was your fault, you wretched beast! Your madness doomed my entire family before I had even taken my first breath! How dare you speak of her past as if you mourn her loss? There is no need for words, wield your weapon as the incarnation of strife and fight!"

Vengeance does not heal wounds, but right now, it is all he desires. He hates Nikador with pure, unwavering intensity, and this hatred has become so potent that if he doesn't purge it, it will consume him.

The incarnation only laughs, a cruel, grating sound. "Thy hatred is as clear as day, Mydeimos. These words must have cut deep. It's become quite obvious why thou chose to kill thy father, yet allowed thy signet to sink to the bottom of the Sea of Souls, refusing the people of Kremnos the glory of their past. This is why thou slew the titan of strife, yet allowed the Coreflame to sit, rejected.

"Thou art a failure. Thy weakness is in thine essence itself. Shame, such deep shame! A proud legacy has been reduced to the whorish omega!"

"My birth did not destroy this legacy you speak of, it is the legacy itself! Endless strife is an ether that has intoxicated our people for a thousand years, and you are the poisoner!"

"If that is what thou believe, then prove thyself! O child abandoned by both fate and honor, show me what thou art capable of, and put out the flames of thine own destiny!"

"... I will rip your chest asunder, titan, just as I did to the former king. If you took everything from me, then I shall take what matters most from you."

"Then ignite the flames of thy fears and step onto the battlefield! Either thou shalt consume me, or I shall reduce thee to ash in the heat of glorious combat! Remember this, Mydeimos: the son of Gorgo will be crowned in blood! The moment I die, thou shalt ascend!"

Mydei snaps.

He roars as he charges toward the nearest Titankin, his fist connecting with its head and shattering it before his rational mind can even process what he's doing. He isn't in control of himself anymore, he is under the bloodlust's behest. The pounding in his skull is now an endless war cry, fragmenting his psyche and overriding every sense of self-preservation.

Each strike of his gauntlets against an enemy brings the slightest bit of relief that is then immediately overpowered by the raging torrent within his soul. All he can do is shed more tainted ichor. He must fight until Nikador's lifeblood has all been drained, and his greatest enemy is finally felled.

Distantly, he hears Stelle and Dan Heng saying something, but it doesn't register. He can only hear his own harsh breathing amidst that infernal chanting. Another Titankin, another, another--it isn't enough. Nothing will satiate him, or quiet that voice.

The warriors endlessly gravitating toward him are unrelenting, no matter how many he kills. Ichor is spilled in such quantities that the ground beneath him shines gold. The fire within him burns brighter, hotter, stronger.

It is unbearable. This is his worst nightmare come true. He is losing his mind, and when he reclaims the Coreflame, there will be nothing left but this unquenchable thirst for wanton violence. He cannot even save himself, there is no chance for him to save his child from this fate.

They do not deserve this, oh gods, they do not deserve the terrible thing he will become. Nobody does. The Kremnoans will follow him through his

madness, just as they follow Nikador, and they will all die. He cannot save them, he cannot resist the temptation of his brutal destiny.

He delivers a devastating uppercut to a Titankin's head, reveling in the cracking of stone just as nausea rises in his throat. Grabbing its limp body, he tosses it into another, and watches, elated and disgusted, as their ichor coats the walls. He swipes his tongue across his lips, tasting what has stained them, and the blood is as sweet and revolting as any nectar.

It is all too much. He can't do this, it is too perfect for him and it is so, so wrong--

Behind him, he hears the thud of a foot landing on tile. He whips around, ready to tackle his next foe, but instead, pain lances through his lower abdomen, so sudden that he cannot suppress a groan.

A sword is lodged in his womb, and the one holding it is Phainon.

Mydei awakens with a strangled cry, hands flying to grasp at the swell of his abdomen. Cold sweat coats his body. His heart is beating so quickly that it's making him feel sick.

"The child," he gasps, frantic. The place where he was impaled has healed over, but that does not mean the child has healed, as he still does not know if they are--

"Lord Mydei, it's alright!" somebody shouts, and he looks up to find Castorice staring down at him. Behind her is the familiar ceiling of the Chrysos Heirs's private lounge. It seems he's been laid down on one of the couches against the wall.

"... Oh."

It wasn't real, of course. The child isn't in any danger. He wasn't actually impaled, Phainon only did it to snap him out of his mindless bloodlust. But that revelation does not unburden him of all his concerns.

"Is Phainon back?" he asks, scrambling to his feet so quickly that he nearly knocks his head against Castorice's.

"Yes, he reappeared at the same time you did, and the outsiders followed right behind. All of you were unconscious--the outsiders came to before you did, but Lord Phainon is still out--"

On a nearby bed, he's lying prone atop the sheets, as pale as a specter. Aglaea is seated beside him, two fingers pressed against the pulse point of his neck. His hackles raise at the intermixing of her scent with Phainon's-- foolish, really, to be bothered by another alpha's scent, but his pregnancy has made his instincts harder to ignore.

"How is he?" he asks, as he approaches the bedside. Phainon's face is ashen, and he cannot resist the urge to reach out and card his fingers through his hair, though he does resist the urge to bury his face in the crook of his neck.

He looks terribly unwell. Even asleep, his face is twisted in discomfort. His breathing is uneven, almost frantic. Mydei pulls back, frowning.

"Ah, you're awake," Aglaea greets. "Lord Phainon seems to be fine, at least physically, and Trinnon reports that his soul is whole and hale. With ample rest for both body and mind, he'll be up in no time."

Mydei exhales a breath he didn't realize he was holding. "Good."

"Based on what the outsiders told us, it seems the trial forces one to face the greatest fear in the depths of their heart... So, Lord Phainon must have had to relive his past, when he watched his homeland be devoured by the Black Tide," Castorice says, voice tinged with sadness.

"In all likelihood, he did. I saw images from my own past, but warped into something even more dreadful. I can only imagine what he saw. The Black Tide is an evil incomparable to any other."

"Is the Black Tide really so scary? Dan Heng and I have heard you all talk about it so much, but we don't actually know what it is," Stelle says from her place on another couch, seated beside Dan Heng.

Aglaea is quick to explain, as always. "It is a source of madness in this world, an unspeakable... thing that is as relentless as any plague. It appeared alongside the three titans of trickery. Nobody knows where it came from, all we know is that it is steadily encroaching upon Amphoreus, surrounding this tranquil city much like the tides--that is why it got its name.

"Those who succumb to it lose all wit and humanity, becoming nothing more than monstrous husks. No creature is immune, even gods and titans cannot escape its clutches."

"Though Nikador is an embodiment of calamity, they are meant to bear the responsibility of fending it off," Castorice adds, "which is perhaps why Lord Phainon threw himself into the Trial of Nikador so readily."

"But now, we must look for other methods of reigniting the flames of strife," Aglaea concludes, before casting her gaze to Mydei. "If it were as simple as emerging triumphant on the battlefield, the Kremnoans would have already been fighting against the Black Tide in Nikador's stead. Of course, it is not that simple. One must bear the heavy crown of divinity."

Mydei glowers at her, now lacking the patience for niceties. "It is a decision I cannot make in haste, do not lecture me. There is still more I must do."

"I simply mean to encourage you to consider your next steps--"

"I'm leaving."

Nobody tries to stop him. If they did, he thinks he'd try to strangle them.

He makes his way across the palace, without a clear destination in mind. As he wanders, he is acutely aware of the stares he's getting--he's no longer making any efforts to hide his pregnancy, and having donned his regular garb once more, it is glaringly obvious. He ignores them all. He has much more important worries than his public image.

Whatever the people think of him has no bearing on what he does next. It's not like they've ever loved him, they've simply tolerated his presence. As

for the other Kremnoans, they look upon them with much less respect. He is a Chrysos Heir, while they are just brutes hungry for their next battle.

After all these years, that sentiment has not changed much. He thinks he's begun to understand why.

Eventually, he finds himself leaned against the railing of an observation point, looking over the sprawling cityscape of Okhema. It has become his home now, much more familiar to him than his birthplace, which he has only seen in ruin. Whatever beauty it once held is gone. Regret is all that remains.

Just as he detests Nikador, he detests Castrum Kremnos. That city is a temple for a merciless titan, one who has groomed their people into believing death is something to be cherished more than life. The gilded marble is a facade for a deep, terrible sickness. His people think of it as their home, unwilling to accept that there is something better, kinder for them in this world.

A stray palm comes to rest upon his swollen abdomen as he sighs to himself. He wishes his child could grow up here, in these joyous and vibrant streets, surrounded by other children who dream of life, not its end.

But that wish is dead. The child will go where he goes, and he doesn't think he has much time left here. A plan is beginning to take shape in his mind--it is not a pleasant one, but it may be the thing to save his people, even if he himself is lost to strife.

Before that, though, he requires a confirmation.

"... I know you've been following me, Tribbie," he mutters, and she squeaks in fear behind him.

"Sorry! We just had to ask you something! But we know you're worried about Snowy, so it can wait--"

"I'm not worried."

"Oh... we assumed you were, since we know he's very special to you."

"... My apologies, that was rude. But I'm not worried about him, he will certainly pull through. That fool has endured worse."

Mydei does not know the extent of his suffering, but it is much deeper than a simple trial. Failure is one thing. Loss is another.

She giggles. "It's alright, being straightforward suits you better. Congratulations, by the way! We're all excited to meet your baby! We'll make you a cute gift to give them, and we can plan a baby shower for you too! If you need advice, we know a lot about children!"

"Err, that will be unnecessary... Thank you, regardless."

"Aww, okay. Can we ask you about the trial, if you're up for it? We wanted to know what you saw."

"I saw something that terrifies me. It's quite ironic, I'm aware, but that is the truth."

"Do you think you stand a chance against it?"

As he expected, this is why she followed him. He takes a deep breath, and tamps down his rage. He will not raise his voice at Tribbie, not like he did with Aglaea. She was right anyway, it was foolish of him to run.

Truly, it is time for this farce to end, and for him to stop dragging his feet.

"I see why you're questioning me now. This is just the next step in your plan, is it not?"

She cocks her head, feigning innocence. "What plan?"

"Phainon was always going to fail, and I was always going to be the one to reclaim Nikador's Coreflame. You knew all along, even though you didn't attempt to stop him. All you wished to do was buy me time to strengthen my resolve."

"Looks like you know everything, huh..."

"I'm not upset, don't make that face. The Flamechase journey is no game, I am fully aware, and I do not hold it against you for plotting. Somebody needs to reclaim the Coreflame of Strife urgently, or we may lose Oronyx and Cerces to the Black Tide. You've given me all the time you could, and now, it is time for me to meet my destiny."

"So, are you ready?"

"No. I do not hold the key to completing the trial. If I wish to conquer my fear, I must speak with my fellow Kremnoans. It won't take long, I promise."

"... Your people wish for you to become king, right? You're their hero, the only thing that's kept their spirits up since they had to flee to Okhema. Once you ascend, they'll happily follow you, and do whatever you wish."

"Perhaps I was once their hero, but... Lady Tribios, therein lies my greatest fear."

Without another word, he turns his back to her, and walks back to the palace. He doesn't have any more time to waste, there is one person with whom he wishes to converse above all others.

"Krateros, I'd like a word."

He finds his old master near the Verax Leo in the bathhouse, looking off into the verdant gardens grown wild under the eternal sunlight. Even after so many years, Krateros is as fit as ever, though one of his eyes is slowly losing its function; Okhema's healers tried to slow its decline after a grievous injury, but the damage was already done. It is milky white now, the edges of the iris blending into the sclera.

"Ah, Mydeimos. I will provide my counsel as... always..."

When Krateros turns to face Mydei properly, he trails off, stunned. His gaze is fixed on his midsection, and his mouth hangs open.

"Do not gawk at me. Have you never seen an expectant male omega?"

He quickly schools his expression. "Certainly not, I just... I didn't think you'd find somebody to court, much less settle down with. Nobody else could hope to match your prowess and be worthy of your hand in marriage, or so I thought."

The babe was an accident, but Krateros does not need to know of this fact. Whether it was his intention or not, the truth of the matter is the same. Phainon is the only one he will lay with now.

"There is one whose skill is equal to mine."

"Indeed? If so, I'm glad to see you've found happiness in some form. Your mother would be overjoyed, I can only imagine how she'd feel. Ah, the festivities we'd have for the next heir of Kremnos... They would be grander than the ones we had when she was carrying you. How many gifts there would be for you and the young babe, and how lavish they would be!"

"... I do not have time to discuss this right now."

"Sorry, it's too easy to get lost in the past. How shall I advise you?"

"I wish to discuss the future of the Kremnoans."

"Hmm, how interesting, I thought you might come to ask about this. I heard the Coreflame was returned, and yet, you still have not reclaimed its power. Some even say that you plan to give it up. Is this true?"

"Those rumors are not entirely groundless."

"You mean to say that you've entertained the thought of giving up the throne, and forsaking your people?"

There is a hint of anger is Krateros's voice, just as he anticipated. Mydei chooses his next words carefully. "The divine power is not equivalent to the throne. Our people need not follow the path of strife--"

"Enough with the word games!" he barks suddenly. "You, of all people, should understand the plight of our people! Think of the detachment, and all the people who left their homes to follow you, believing in your future! Only memories of the past have kept us alive all these years!"

"There is more to life--"

"Don't be ridiculous! Perhaps these foolish Okhemans believe that strife is unimportant, but it is our lifeblood. If the people lose you... Imagine the disgrace it would bring upon your departed mother, Mydeimos. She died for you, to end Eurypon's schemes, to restore the glory of Castrum Kremnos! Now, the child you carry within you is a gift--a new heir to continue our legacy!"

"... Who is responsible for my father's death, Krateros?"

"Do you think I've gone senile and forgotten that glorious moment? You drove the spear into his heart with your own two hands."

"That was merely the final outcome. How do you not yet see it? It is strife that brought us to that point, strife that killed my mother, strife that drove the Kremnoans from their home. Our principle tenant 'valorous death before triumphant return'... why? Why do we place death on a pedestal? Why do we not yearn for life with the same fervor?"

Krateros scoffs, contempt etched into the hard lines of his face. "Gorgo, the great founder of Castrum Kremnos, was your mother's namesake. I swore to her that I'd guard your crown with my life... I never thought you'd be the first to turn your back on the Kremnoan spirit. It's in your blood, and nourishes the child within you."

"That is what you believe, but I'm not sure if it's the truth," Mydei spits back, a protective hand guarding the place where his child rests. "I do not wish for their fate to be determined by a dead god. Nothing is set in stone."

"Do not be naive. The throne has always been waiting for a worthy king such as yourself. Do not fault me for withholding my loyalty if you refuse it, and doom us all."

"It appears you are not yet ready to discuss the future of our people, then."

"Go down the path you deem to be correct. I know I cannot change your mind once it is set. Just don't renounce our traditions, and know that the people of Kremnos will always be bound to strife. There are things in this world that you cannot hope to alter."

"Tradition does not matter in this era of destruction. If I must burn it to the ground, then I shall."

"My young lord, bear in mind that you should not reveal your vulnerabilities to anyone. If one has the strength to dominate, they should. Do not stoop to frolicking with your prey."

"... You sound like my father. If you only see strength in dominion, then you are no better than him."

"Do not compare me to--"

"Listen to yourself speak!" he roars, voice shaking with rage. "Do you not hear the cruelty in your words? Do you think you're better than him when you only care about the same damn things? No! You have had the chance to redefine yourself, and yet you've decided to remain a coward! Get out of my sight!"

Since he met Krateros in the detachment, Mydei has always looked up to him as a source of wisdom and sound counsel. He trained him in the handling of all varieties of weapons, and as he began to realize the power gifted to him by his heritage, Krateros taught him how to control it. In some ways, he was a parent. Orphaned and alone, his master was the one to transform him from a traumatized child, fresh from seven years of agony in the Sea of Souls, to a capable warrior.

It is a terrible shame to burn another bridge, but if he is to defy fate, then he will do it. Becoming a demigod requires unbearable sacrifice. Very few have the strength, and that is why Aglaea hand-picked him for his role.

And yet, he still does not know what, exactly, he should do. Only one other person may provide him with the clarity he needs, and that person is currently unconscious.

When Phainon wakes, they will have much to discuss. He can only hope that it will not break them both.

Chapter Notes

Three days later, at the beginning of action hour, Phainon wakes.

Mydei is lounging on an armchair dragged next to his bedside, holding a book that he isn't giving much attention, when he hears Phainon let out a low groan. Immediately, he jumps into action, grabbing a blanket to obscure his form and then hurrying to sit on the mattress beside him.

Phainon squints against the light streaming in through the window, expression twisted in discomfort, eyes darting around uncertainly. He reminds Mydei of a cornered animal, one desperate for escape.

"Welcome back to the world of the living," Mydei says, hoping the sound of a familiar voice will bring him to his senses. It seems to work. Phainon relaxes against the bed, tension vanishing.

"What... what happened?" he asks in a ragged voice. "Did I fail?"

"Yes. I had to remove you from the trial, or you were going to die."

They've spent the last few days doing menial things like that. Mydei has tried his best to savor every moment, to stretch out the hours left with he man he loves so dearly, but he knows he cannot linger any longer.

A new battlefield awaits him, and he will fight alone.

"That's not what I mean. It's time for me to leave Okhema."

"Oh. You're going home now, aren't you?"

"Yes. I do not believe I'll be returning to Okhema ever again. So, I believe it is best if we end things."

It is the worst sentence he has ever had to utter. He had to practice saying it a hundred times just to be able to manage it with an even tone.

Oh, how he despises himself for it. It is so, so cruel. Phainon offered up his heart and Mydei is crushing that idyllic dream of love in the span of a breath.

But it's for the best.

If he tells Phainon he no longer loves him, then he'll be free to continue his life without the burden of Mydei's absence haunting him. Painfully but quickly--that is how wounds are treated on the battlefield, and it is how Mydei will do this.

When he receives no response, Mydei stands, and takes the first few steps to the door.

"End things... between us?"

Phainon has risen to his feet, as if to follow him, but he's frozen in place. He seems entirely lost, all his usual confidence melting away into shock.

"Yes."

The pure, agonizing anguish that overtakes his features yanks the air right from Mydei's chest.

Godsdamnit, this is impossible.

"The Coreflame has changed me. I am no longer the person you fell in love with. You shouldn't waste your energy on me, it will only agonize you. The affection I feel for you is rapidly fading. Soon, I will feel nothing at all."

He hopes it will be enough. He needs it to be enough, so Phainon can forget him.

"... Has anybody ever told you that you're a terrible liar?"

Of course, Phainon has always been able to read him with ease.

"I'm simply trying to make this easier for you."

"You don't need to. I'll be okay, I will. If you really want to end things, that's alright, but... Be honest with me, please. All I want is the truth."

"I just thought... By the hells, I don't know. I thought it was for the best. Isn't this worse? To know what I have become, and what I must do, but love me regardless?"

"Even if loving you is the hardest thing in the world, I'll do it without hesitation, Mydei."

"But will you be able to handle my absence? I do not believe that I will return to Okhema ever again, as I said."

"Wait, you... you're serious about leaving?"

"I must fend off the Black Tide now that Nikador is dead. It is my new duty."

Phainon crumples. His entire body seems to slacken, as if all his energy has been suddenly sucked out. His knees buckle; he grabs Mydei's drape, claws at his shoulders for purchase, leaves deep red marks in his skin in his desperation. Mydei reaches down to catch him before he can hit the ground.

"Please don't go, please don't leave me too," he chokes, between sobs and hitching breaths. "I can't lose you, please."

"Phainon, I..."

"I need you, Mydei, I can't--I can't do this, I'm sorry, please stay. I'll do anything, I'll be better, I'll be whatever you want me to be, just don't go."

Mydei does not know what to say anymore, so instead, he lowers them both to the tile floor, slowly, and holds him close.

His breathing gets more erratic, and he begins to curl up on himself. "I know I'm being selfish, I'm sorry, I'm ruining everything, I'm sorry--"

"You can cry, do not be ashamed."

He does, for a long, long time. He seems to lose control of himself--his fingers lock around anything they can find, squeezing, tangling in Mydei's hair, almost pulling, but the sting is bearable. That is not the difficult part, no. The sounds he makes are so dreadful, and Mydei feels his heart cracking into pieces, because he is still human in the ways that matter the most.

Being stabbed in his back would not hurt as badly as this, he thinks. To hold Phainon as he bitterly weeps, wracked by sobs so powerful that they jerk his entire frame, knowing that he is the cause of his anguish--this is some sort of nightmare he wouldn't dare to imagine otherwise.

It feels so wrong. He despises it all. Damn the Fates for choosing this path for him. Why must he suffer like this? Why must Phainon endure more than he already has?

Mydei wants to offer some comfort, anything to make Phainon happy again, but even if he knew what to say, there is a tightness in the back of throat that he knows will turn into tears. All he can do is hold him in silence.

Eventually, Phainon's sobs quiet down to hiccups and sniffles, he extracts himself from their embrace, enough to cradle the swell of Mydei's midsection. His expression is fractured. His eyes are bloodshot and red-rimmed, his lips are quivering, and tear tracks stain his cheeks.

"I only just learned of them, and now... now I have to say goodbye. Gods... Will you send me pictures of them when they are born, at least?"

"... I will not allow you to miss their birth. A kinder world awaits us, our reunion will not be too late. You will be a part of their life, I am certain."

It is terribly naive to make such a declaration, but Mydei wants it to be true with such fervor, and he cannot consider the other possibilities, not right now.

"Can I come visit, then?"

"I don't know," he says carefully. "It isn't safe in Castrum Kremnos--it won't be for many months to come. But if there comes a day when I have beaten back the Black Tide enough to afford me some freedom, then I shall call for you."

"And you'll message me with your teleslate?"

"Whenever I am able."

Phainon lets out a shaky breath. "Okay, that's... okay."

Mydei kisses him softly, tasting the salt of his tears on his lips. They linger like that for ages, in the warmth of their embrace, Phainon's hands still resting over his womb.

"... I must leave," Mydei whispers, when he can bear it no longer.

"I know. Damnit, I know. Can I give you one last thing, at least?"

"Of course."

Phainon digs into his pocket and produces a small golden ring. It is polished to a beautiful luster, and brilliantly reflects the light shining through the open window. He picks up Mydei's right hand, bare of its gauntlet, and carefully slides it onto his ring finger.

On its face is a carved symbol that Mydei would recognize in a heartbeat. He stares at it for what feels like an eternity, completely stunned.

"This is my mother's signet ring. How...?"

"It took a very long time to find... I've spent the last year searching, I think. Chartonus helped a lot, and he helped me fix it when we finally fished it up. I really only did the last round of polishing."

"I see," Mydei forces out. "This is... It means a lot to me. I shall wear it with pride. Thank you."

"I'm glad I could find it."

Slowly, painfully, Mydei stands. "Does that settle everything?"

"I guess it does, huh."

"... Farewell, my love."

"Farewell, my love."

Mydei walks out the door, and does not look back. His eyes remain trained at the horizon as he passes the city gates, marches away from the safety of Kephale's light, crosses the endless darkness of the Evernight, parting the sea of enemies with mindless ease.

It is only once he has reached his new throne, built from mighty crystals of his own power, that he turns back to face the world behind him.

The son of Gorgo will be crowned in blood.

"Mother, I'm home."
